**Finding: missing** (medium severity) — no reciprocal transition assistance or data return in our favour.

**What the document has:** Article XIV (Effect of Termination) is an extensive wind-down regime, but it is entirely one-directional. Ono must transition clinical/pre-clinical studies (14.2(a)(i)), continue distributing through the Wind-down Period (14.2(a)(ii)), assign Regulatory Filings and hand over all Data and Ono Know-How (14.2(a)(iii)), grant back licences (14.2(a)(v)), deliver up or destroy Array's Materials and Confidential Information within 90 days (14.2(a)(vi)), and assign trademarks, domains and Sublicences (14.2(a)(vii)–(viii)). The only bilateral language is the general cooperation covenant in 14.2(a)(iv), and it is directed at transitioning the Product back to Array.

**The gap:** Article X contains no return/destruction mechanic, and "destroy" appears nowhere else in the agreement — so Array has no obligation to return or delete our Data or Confidential Information on termination, and no committed transition assistance or continued supply while we remain obliged to distribute Product. That falls short of even the fallback position (90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days).

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** new Section 14.2(a)(x) inserted after 14.2(a)(ix) requiring Array to (A) provide up to six months' transition assistance including continued Article IX supply while we must keep distributing, (B) return our Data and Confidential Information in machine-readable format within 30 days of request, and (C) certify deletion thereafter. The carve-out preserves Array's agreed rights to Data and Ono Know-How under 14.2(a)(iii), (v) and (ix), so the commercial bargain is not reopened; the comment offers the 90-day fallback.
